8m1v13:385: The evolution from V1 to V2 is essentially a paradigm shift in Agent system architecture. V1 adopted a distributed multi-agent architecture, breaking the task into five specialized subtasks: knowledge extraction Agent, loss analysis Agent, verification & defense Agent, output monitoring Agent, and metric monitoring Agent. This design was reasonable when model capabilities were weaker—early models had limited context windows (4K) and unstable instruction following, so tasks needed to be split and handled by different agents separately. However, as the context window of large models expanded from 4K to 128K and then to 1M+, instruction following and autonomous execution capabilities improved dramatically, and this splitting became a bottleneck instead. The information loss and coordination overhead introduced by the orchestration layer exceeded the problems it solved. More importantly, multi-agent orchestration architecture cannot enjoy the dividends of rapid model iteration—the orchestration logic and inter-agent message protocols are hard-coded. Even when the underlying model capability improves significantly, the upper orchestration layer still performs fixed-granularity information trimming and process constraints, so model capability gains are "truncated" by the architecture design. The core changes in V2 are reflected in four dimensions:
